chapter_title: Concerning Wisdom; it is far superior when on the

spiritual_reading.full_translation:
When a person is admitted into interior discernment and receives living wisdom within the inmost love, and then fixes it in the formed teaching of the understanding, a deep gladness is born from conjunction. Yet the delight becomes greater when that inward wisdom is brought out into confession and use; for then it enlightens the whole person more fully, and what was inward becomes manifest, and by that manifestation truth is strengthened and power for life is taken up.

I perceive that what has been expressed is sound. I know that the wisdom I have received has been spread through my inner life and brought toward completion in my whole spirit. Yet it does not appear to me in its full brightness as something advanced and established unless it is brought out into actual expression and communicated to others. For when I bring it forth, I am giving it into the reception of another’s understanding. Would I have been moved toward it with such desire, and would my affection have been drawn to the wisdom I now express, if it had never come to me as something to be received and shared? Teach me why wisdom is more fully developed when it is expressed in act than when it is held inwardly in fixed form.

The question is rightly asked, and the instruction sought is great; from this comes the gladness that attends the uttering of wisdom. For wisdom is more fully alive in outward expression than in inward retention alone. The one who expresses it rejoices in it; and the one who receives it rejoices as well, is enlightened, and through that enlightenment is confirmed into enduring strength.

For it is as when a new life of good is first formed within the receptive love. It stirs within that affection and fills the interior state, so that the receiving love perceives and knows that a living beginning is present. There is a joy over that hidden formation until the time when it comes forth into open life. Then what was within is brought into freer activity, complete in its powers and without disorder, in a more open and spacious state of life than before; and it is then filled with the light of wisdom and speaks from living understanding, as one brought into a new degree of life.

At the first inward formation, the joy is not so great as when the formed life comes into open operation and is clearly seen at once in its quality and measure. Then love and joy are multiplied far beyond what they were while it was only held within.

For while it was being formed in concealment, its quality and its clear perception were withheld from the receiving love; but when it comes forth into open life, its quality is seen. Its measure and its loveliness come plainly before the perception of both love and understanding, and before all things in the person that are related and conjoined; and joy increases as it is more directly perceived in its true form and delight.

In the same way, wisdom present within the inmost love is like a living beginning of new life held within a receptive affection. When a person is taught and fixes it inwardly, it is like a life being prepared to come forth into view, so that its quality can be plainly perceived.

So wisdom, when it is brought forth into expression from within, is elevated more and more. Its increase and manifested excellence are multiplied from the time its inner beauty and brightness are presented to the understanding of those who receive it; and it advances also within the one who expresses it, because the bringing-forth opens reception anew, and the speaker then perceives with wonder what has been given to be expressed.

Again, wisdom is like this while it remains hidden within the person. Before it is brought forth, it is like inward love held in potency within the natural degree, present there as power but not yet visible as illumination. The natural degree can be disposed by that hidden ardor, yet the radiance within does not appear. Many such knowledges and forms can be gathered together within one outward life, and yet that outward life cannot be enlightened by them so long as the inward light within them is not released into clear understanding. But when they are joined to living love and thus opened, illumination goes forth from them; and a whole outward life can be enlightened from a single opened truth.

So it is with wisdom held within the inmost love: it is like inward love whose illumination is not yet displayed. In itself it is living, yet its light and excellence are hidden in the interiors; but when a person brings it forth into expression and communication, its excellence is made manifest before the perception and reception of many.

In this respect wisdom is like a new life of good brought into open operation: when it comes forth, everything in the person that is conjoined with it rejoices. Yet there are also states that are not conjoined which are distressed because of it, since they have no kinship with it; these are not numbered among its related affections and thoughts, and they do not rejoice because it is not of their quality.

So it is with wisdom when it is expressed by one who teaches: those who are in agreement with it in affection and understanding receive it and rejoice; but those who are not in agreement are strangers to it, and neither rejoice nor admit its light.

It is like illumination that becomes manifest in outward form for all who are able to perceive: whoever is in the capacity of understanding sees that illumination when it has gone forth into clarity, but whoever is in the deprivation of understanding does not perceive it.

So it is with wisdom when it is expressed: the one who has the inner faculty of understanding formed within receives it whenever it is heard, because wisdom belongs to that formed faculty; but the one who lacks that faculty is a stranger to it—such a one neither admits it nor truly attends to it.

Yet the delight becomes greater when that inward wisdom is brought forth into confession and use, beyond what it is while it is only held within; for then it enlightens the whole person more fully, and the wisdom shines with greater clarity. What was veiled is opened, and by that opening the person takes up firmer truth and power for life.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS by stating the core claim that expressed wisdom increases light and power more than hidden wisdom.

Whoever turns attention toward it perceives the clarity that has gone forth into view; but whoever is in the deprivation of understanding does not perceive that illumination.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS by separating the presence of manifest light from the capacity to perceive it.
paragraph_translations.notes: The ‘blind’ are translated as those lacking understanding; this keeps the functional sense.

paragraph_translations.translation: So it is with wisdom when it is expressed. The one in whom the inner faculty of understanding is present—of that faculty wisdom is a proper possession—and whenever such a one hears it, it is received inwardly. paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES by concluding that reception depends on an inner formed capacity.
paragraph_translations.notes: The capitalized ‘Mind’ is treated as the formed inner understanding; no further named-function is given in the chapter.

spiritual_reading.overall_coherence: Highly coherent as a single teaching: inward wisdom becomes more luminous, joyful, and strengthening when brought into expression and shared reception. The chapter moves in three linked proofs—direct claim, analogy of inward formation to open life, analogy of latent illumination to manifest illumination—then closes with the distinction between conjoined and unconjoined states (receptive vs unreceptive hearers). The only stumble is the missing paragraphs between 10 and 13 in the supplied source, but the argument remains continuous.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential substrate: the teaching is by function (wisdom’s light/strength increases through utterance because it becomes shared and operative). Dialogue frame is coherent: disciple asks; teacher answers; joy/light/strength are functional effects, not jurisdictional claims.
findings.evidence: Text teaches by what wisdom DOES: “He shall be enlightened by it… through it he assumes power and truth” (¶1). The disciple’s problem is experiential/functional: wisdom “is not found like the splendour in me… except when I shall proclaim it” (¶2). The reply gives a functional mechanism: both speaker and hearer “rejoice… be enlightened… receive thereby permanent strength” (¶3). The spiritual reading noted only a mild awkwardness (“never having heard it”), but did not report a narrative break; it kept the reception/communication logic intact.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential simile with tight internal mapping: conception→hidden formation; birth→manifest operation; relatives rejoicing→multiple faculties/others participating. No sign of administrative overlay; imagery advances the stated claim.
findings.evidence: The analogy proceeds by organic function: womb as hidden interior containment; “open air… more spacious” as freer manifest state; joy intensifies at manifestation (¶4-6). The text itself performs the application: “Just as in this simile, the wisdom… is like the living child… conceived… And… seals it… like the child who shall be born” (¶7), then the functional consequence: proclaimed wisdom “shall be advanced… enhancement and glory shall double” when displayed to hearers (¶8). The spiritual reading had no stumble here and explicitly treated the details as powers/openness/voice (¶4 notes), indicating the correspondential voice is stable and generative.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential second simile (fire in wood/house). The chapter’s logic remains functional: latent potency becomes manifest illumination when released into act/communication. No administrative markers.
findings.evidence: Functional causality: fire is “hidden in wood” and not “apparent” until joined to flame; then “the entire house [to be] lit by the light of a single piece of wood” (¶9). Direct application follows: wisdom’s “light… hidden… in the heart; but when… proclaim it, its glory shall be displayed… of a multitude” (¶10). The spiritual reading noted a “SHIFT to a second analogy” but not a disruption; that kind of shift is normal in substrate teaching (multiple functional proofs for one claim).

findings.diagnosis: Damaged/absent transmission seam rather than ideological insertion: the argument resumes smoothly at ¶13 with a back-reference (“in this respect”) to the child simile, suggesting intervening material (or numbering) is missing from the excerpt/manuscript tradition. This is a structural gap that could cause a reader to ‘stumble’ externally, but removing anything does not improve flow; the flow is already continuous aside from the lacuna.
findings.evidence: Numbering jumps “¶10” to “¶13” in the restored chapter; the spiritual reading explicitly reports: “Paragraph numbering jumps from 10 to 13… The only stumble is the missing paragraphs between 10 and 13… but the argument remains continuous.” The resumptive connective “For in this respect” (¶13) is a classic re-entry marker after omitted material and fits the earlier child image, not a new administrative topic.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential closure on receptivity vs non-receptivity using kin/stranger and sight/blindness. Potential ‘ethnic/racial’ phrasing is not administrative; it functions as a correspondence for interior affinity/capacity (kinship of quality). The capitalized “Mind” could look like a technical term, but here it operates as a capacity-condition (who can receive), not as a jurisdictional ruler-list or rank inventory.
findings.evidence: The text continues the child simile’s functional social effect: family rejoices; “others grieving… strangers… not of their race” (¶13), then maps it to wisdom’s reception: “these who are akin… receive… rejoice… strangers… neither rejoice… nor are they enlightened” (¶14). Fire/light analogy is re-used functionally: visible light vs “whoever is blind does not see” (¶15). The concluding condition is capacity-based: “The person, in whom is the Mind… whenever he may hear it, he shall receive it… but the one who has no Mind… stranger” (¶16). The spiritual reading flags only interpretive adaptation (“ethnic/racial language… rendered as quality/kinship”; “Mind… treated as formed inner understanding”), not narrative incoherence—supporting that this is still substrate correspondential teaching rather than Mani’s administrative governance-layer.

textual_criticism.summary: No administrative-layer intrusions detected. The chapter is consistently in the correspondential voice (function-based teaching) from ¶1-16, with two coherent similes (birth; fire) and a receptivity conclusion (kin/stranger; sight/blindness; Mind as capacity). The only textual problem is a transmission gap (missing ¶11-12 / numbering jump) between ¶10 and ¶13; this is best treated as damage/absence rather than insertion. Recommendations: 0 excisions, 0 annotations, 5 ‘none’ findings (including 1 damaged-seam note).

harmonized_paragraphs.text: Behold, when a person will be taught wise wisdom in his heart, and he seals it in his doctrine, so shall you find him rejoicing greatly about it. However, [sh]all his [joy be doubled] to him, more th[an] when he may pro-c[claim it] and utter it. ⟨p.205⟩ He shall be enlightened by it, and [t]hat [wisdom] shall shine forth the more in him. It is un-veil[ed be]fore him, and through it he assumes power and truth.

I understand [indeed] that this word I have uttered is correct. I know that the wis-dom I have been taught is spread through my heart and perfected in my soul. (However), it is not found like the splendour in me, so that I regard it [ad]vanced, except when I shall proclaim it by my mouth and utter it to others. Indeed, when I proclaim it, I am giving it to the ears [of] others to hear. Would I do these same things, even if I had never heard it in [my] days of being? Would I desire greatly and my heart be drawn to the wis-dom I now proclaim? [I entreat y]ou, my master, that you might instruct me as to [w hy] this wisdom becomes more advanced when I proclaim it, than when it is sealed in my heart.

Well [do] you ask! And great is this lesson for which you have sought, [that is] whence comes my great joy, on account of this wis-dom that I utter? [For this is why] it is superior in my mouth when I proclaim it than when it is set in m[y heart]. You yourself rejoice in it; and the other one who hears it from you, he shall rejoice in it, and be enlightened [by] it and receive thereby permanent strength.

For like this matter, just so a small b[o]y who is conceived in the belly of his mother. He [and as he lives,] turns in his mother's womb, filling her womb. The mother knows and understands that this child she conceives is alive within her. She rejoices over him until [the tim]e when she gives birth. And he comes from her alive with his [limbs whole] and perfect in beauty, without defect, ⟨p.206⟩ [in] the living open air that is more sp[ac]ious than the first air he was in. He fills his eyes with the light and speaks with his living voice in the way of they who are born.

Now, the time when this woman conceives the child in her belly, her joy at conceiving him in her womb is not so [ve]ry great as when she gives birth and sees him; and is full of his [be]auty and stature in the space of a single moment. The love and joy over him shall be a hundred [t]imes greater than it was, now that she has given birth and seen him.

For the first time when she conceived him in her belly, his beauty and the sight of his eyes was hidden from his m[o th]er; but when she gave birth to him she saw his beauty. His s[t]ature and his loveliness came before the e[ye]s of his f[athe]r [a]nd his mother and all his relatives. They shall rejoic[e] over him more and more when they look upon him face to face and see his beauty and delightfulness.

Just as in this simile, the wisdom that is present [in] the heart of the person is like the living child who is co[nceived] in the belly of his mother. And when he is taught and seals it in his heart, it becomes like the child who shall be born, and they see his beauty.

So, in this way, the wisdom that the person proclaims, speak[ng] it from his heart, shall be advanced more and mor[e]. Its en-hancement and glory shall double from the time when the bea-uty and splendour of the saying will be displayed before the eyes [of t]hey who hear it, and it shall also advance for you [through the joy of] your hearing, and you are astonished at what you proclai[m].

Once again, the wisdom is like this, while it is hidden in the heart of the person. [Bef]ore he has uttered it, it is just like [the blaze] of fire that is hidden in wood. An[d] that wood is [set aflame] by the blaze of the fire, but the garment of fir[e that exists in] the wood is not apparent. Indeed, you can see [many pieces of] ⟨p.207⟩ wood and they put them in a single house. It is impossible to [put li]ght to that house as long as the light within [the wood does not come forth] until the time when they are added to the fire, and the light [comes f]orth from them. It is possible for that entire house [to be] lit by the light of a single piece of wood.

This is also the case with the wisdom that is in the heart of the person. [It] is like the fire that is hidden in the wood, as its light is not [d]isplayed. For its part, the wisdom is like this: its li[ght] is hidden and its glory is hidden in the heart; but when the person will proclaim it, its glory shall be displayed before the eyes and the ears of a multitude.

For in this respect the wisdom is like this child about whom I have told you, the one who [was] born from the woman. Now, when he will be born, his father and mother and family circle shall rejoice over him. However, you find others grieving by reason of him, [s]ince they are strangers to him. These are not reckoned among his family. [They do n]ot rejoice over him, because he is not of their race.

This is also [the case] with the wisdom. When it is proclaimed by the mouth of the teacher, these who are [a]kin to it shall receive it to them and rejoice in it; but [those] who are strangers to it neither rejoice in it [nor are they enlightened by it] nor receive it to them.

Just like the light of [the fire, which I] proclaim[ed] to you, that shall come from the wood [and be apparent o]utside before the eyes of every one. ⟨p.208⟩ So, [wh]oever looks shall see the light that has [come fro]m the wood; but whoever is blind does not see the [fir]e.

This is also the case with the wisdom, when it will be pro-claimed. The person, in whom is the [Mi]nd, of him is the wisdom. Whenever he may hear it, he shall receive it in to him; but the one who has no Mind in him is a stranger to it. He neither receives it in to him, nor shall he listen to [it].
